name: Carnitine Transporter Deficiency (Primary Carnitine Deficiency)

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Primary Carnitine Deficiency

criteria.description: Persistently low free carnitine levels in plasma
Pathogenic variants in the SLC22A5 gene confirmed by molecular genetic testing
Presence of clinical symptoms such as muscle weakness, cardiomyopathy, or hypoglycemia
Reduced carnitine uptake in cultured fibroblasts

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of low serum carnitine, clinical features consistent with the disorder, and confirmation of pathogenic SLC22A5 variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis can be supported by functional assays of carnitine transport in fibroblasts.

pathognomonic.notes: Markedly low plasma free carnitine levels
Hypoglycemia without appropriate ketone body production

common.notes: Enlarged liver due to fat accumulation

occasional.notes: Confusion or altered mental status during metabolic crises
Irregular heart rhythms secondary to cardiomyopathy
Poor growth in infants and children

laboratory: Elevated creatine kinase during rhabdomyolysis episodes
imaging: MRI or ultrasound showing hepatomegaly or hepatic steatosis
genetic: Pathogenic variants in SLC22A5 gene encoding OCTN2 transporter
other: Reduced carnitine uptake in cultured fibroblasts
Improvement of symptoms with carnitine supplementation

distinguishingFeatures: Elevated multiple acylcarnitines on metabolic screening
Different genetic causes (ETFA, ETFB, ETFDH genes)

redFlags: Recurrent hypoketotic hypoglycemia in infancy or childhood
Severe muscle weakness with rhabdomyolysis episodes
references: Longo N, et al. Primary Carnitine Deficiency. In: GeneReviews® [Internet]. University of Washington, Seattle; 2020.
